newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries open higher as tone remains positive.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries open higher as tone remains positive.

text.p: U.S. Treasury prices opened higher on Wednesday, following gains in Tokyo overnight and benefitting from the restoration of a positive tone to the market by reports Tuesday indicating tempered third-quarter economic growth.
The 6-3/4 percent 30-year Treasury bond was up 5/32 to 98-18/32, yielding 6.86 percent, in early trade.
Analysts said buying in Japan overnight extended Tuesday's bond market gains in the U.S.

The Treasury market is benefitting from the positive tone restored to it by economic data released on Tuesday. Most important was the moderate growth picture of the nation's manufacturing sector provided by the National Association of Purchasing Management's (NAPM) September index.

The September NAPM index read 51.7, a shade below economists' consensus forecast of 52.5, and slightly lower than the 52.6 reading in August. A reading above 50 points signals expansion, below 50 -- contraction.
Also, both weekly surveys of chain and department store sales showed declines.
Carl Steen, market analyst at Maria Fiorini Ramirez Inc. said the higher dollar was also providing support to the bond market.
"The stronger dollar is helping to keep the market bid even when there is some bearish data," he said.
One technical factor was also bullish, said Steen.

"The close on Tuesday) was higher than the previous day's high so while we failed (to pierce) strong resistance levels, the close was higher than the high of the day before. And that's a bullish signal," Steen said.
The only piece of economic data the market is due to get is the 1000 EDT/1400 GMT release of the August construction spending report.
Economists surveyed by Reuters offered an average forecast of up 0.8 percent for August construction spending, versus a sharp 1.4 percent decline in July.
Economists said the construction spending data series tends to be volatile. And market movements may be constrained by the looming September U.S payrolls report on Friday.
"We may be trading pretty much sideways until the payrolls number," said Steen.
In early trade, three- and six-month bill rates were each down one basis point to 4.96 percent and 5.13 percent, respectively.
Year-bill rates were also down one basis point to 5.33 percent.

Two-year note prices were up 1/32 to 99-31/32, yielding 6.02 percent. Five-year notes were up 2/32 to 100 even, yielding 6.37 percent. The ten-year notes were up 2/32 to 102-19/32, yielding 6.63 percent.
